blogs.title: The Lean Diabetic Trap: When Young Hyperglycemia Isn't Type 1 or Type 2
blogs.description: A deep dive into the clinical algorithm for distinguishing Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY) from Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes in young, non-obese patients. We discuss the red flags—such as negative autoantibodies, preserved C-peptide, and strong family history—that should trigger genetic testing before committing to a lifelong insulin regimen.

blogs.title: When the Database is Silent: Interpreting Novel Genetic Variants in Diabetes
blogs.description: This post explores the challenge of diagnosing monogenic diabetes when genetic testing reveals a variant not listed in major databases like ClinVar. We walk through the American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) guidelines, the utility of AlphaMissense scores, and how clinical segregation within a family can confirm pathogenicity for novel HNF1A mutations.

blogs.title: Deprescribing Insulin: Precision Pharmacotherapy for HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: Why does a patient with an HbA1c of 10.2% transition from basal insulin to a GLP-1 receptor agonist and metformin? We analyze the therapeutic implications of a confirmed HNF1A-MODY diagnosis, highlighting the superior efficacy of sulfonylureas and GLP-1 agonists in preserving beta-cell function compared to insulin, and the importance of avoiding overtreatment.

blogs.title: The SGLT2 Conundrum: Renal Thresholds and Drug Safety in MODY
blogs.description: HNF1A mutations affect the transcription of SGLT2, leading to glycosuria at lower glucose thresholds. This post explains the pathophysiology behind this finding and discusses the potential risks of prescribing SGLT2 inhibitors to HNF1A-MODY patients, including the danger of severe dehydration and euglycemic DKA due to compounded renal glucose excretion.

blogs.title: One Diagnosis, Three Generations: The Imperative of Cascade Screening
blogs.description: MODY is an autosomal dominant condition, meaning one diagnosis can unlock the medical history of an entire family. We discuss the public health and clinical benefits of cascade genetic screening, how to counsel patients on family testing, and the potential to prevent misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatment in at-risk relatives.
